summary:
Read-only audit of the Health tab (HealthTab, components/health/**, healthAggregate.ts, healthMetrics.ts, api/healthApi.ts, hooks/useHealthExport.ts, Daily HealthCard). `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` is clean. I ran four edge cases against the real healthAggregate module with sucrase, in a scratchpad script only: one minute-grain hour of 3000 steps is counted as 50, an empty hour of heart-rate data returns {min:0,max:0,avg:0}, a sleep night's stage-bar shares add up to 112%, and a heart-rate day with only Avg values returns min 0 / max 0.

WHAT'S WRONG, IN SHORT:
(1) The right-rail HealthStatsPanel always drops today. So Day mode on today shows only dashes, and last night is always missing from the sleep figures.
(2) The same labelled figure ("weekly average") is worked out with different rules in the section headline, the right panel and the Daily card. The numbers side by side disagree.
(3) The Heart day chart falls to 0 bpm for every hour with no data, including every future hour of today.
(4) 'Latest'-type cards such as VO2 max only look inside the selected window, so they read "—" most days. This blocks the owner's main question ("how bad is my VO2?").
(5) The hour-level collapse would wipe out older per-minute data if any is still stored. The code's own comment says the 2026-07-20 samples were per-minute; I could not check the database.
(6) Heavy data fetching. About 21 separate paginated select('*') queries run for the Steps view alone. The right panel downloads twice the window again under a different cache key. The workouts list downloads the full raw payload (heart-rate curves, GPS routes) even while it's collapsed.
(7) Body weight comes from four sources (Apple Health, the smart scale, Hevy, and the Hevy+Apple merge Progress uses). Readers pick different ones, and two "Weight" charts sit in the same card.

The aggregation rules match CLAUDE.md: hour-only collapse for sum metrics, the 90% containment rule for merging sleep sessions, wake-day night attribution, and kJ→kcal for the two energy metrics. The weak spots are around those rules: how "today" is handled, empty hours, minute-grain rows, and pagination ties.

WHAT A STANDALONE /health PAGE SHOULD CONTAIN:
- **Header:** its own route and nav entry with ONE date control. Real calendar options: Today / 7 days / 30 days / 90 days / 1 year. Label them "Last 7 days", not "(this week)".
- **Hero, "How am I doing":** one tile per marker, each with the value, the trend against the previous window, a colour band against a cited reference, and one line saying why it matters. No composite health score, per the house rule. Tiles:
  - Sleep last night + 7-day average vs ≥7 h (AASM/SRS consensus, Watson 2015), plus bedtime/wake-time regularity (Windred 2024, Sleep: regularity predicts mortality more strongly than duration).
  - Resting HR 7-day vs a personal 60-day baseline, plus the clinical 60–100 range (Zhang 2016 CMAJ: about +9% all-cause mortality per +10 bpm).
  - HRV (SDNN) 7-day rolling vs a personal baseline ±1 SD (Plews 2013 approach). Population norms fit Apple's short SDNN readings poorly.
  - Steps 7-day average vs ~7,000–8,000/day, where most of the mortality benefit sits (Paluch 2022 and Ding 2025, both Lancet Public Health).
  - Weekly exercise minutes vs WHO 2020 (150–300 moderate or 75–150 vigorous, plus 2 strength days). The strength days can come from Hevy.
  - VO2 max: latest known value with its date, placed on a FRIEND-registry percentile ladder by age and sex (Kaminsky 2015/2022, Mayo Clin Proc). Context: each +1 MET (3.5 ml/kg/min) is about 13% lower mortality (Kodama 2009 JAMA), and low vs elite fitness is HR ≈5 (Mandsager 2018 JAMA Netw Open). Caveat: Apple's estimate carries roughly 10–15% error and tends to read low for fitter users.
  - Weight shown as a 7-day moving-average trend in kg/week (not first-vs-last raw readings), with body-fat category (ACE, men: fitness 14–17%, average 18–24%) and waist-to-height ratio <0.5 (NICE 2022; waist is already in Hevy measurements).
- **Sections:**
  - Cardio fitness: VO2 max history, Cardio Recovery (1-minute drop ≤12 bpm is abnormal, Cole 1999 NEJM), walking HR.
  - Recovery: resting HR / HRV / respiratory rate (12–20) / SpO2 (95–100%) / wrist temperature as a deviation from the personal baseline, on a shared weekly axis next to training load from Hevy.
  - Sleep: the existing night timeline and stages with the fixed bar, a 7 h reference line, and a consistency chart.
  - Activity: steps, exercise minutes, stand hours, active + basal energy. Hand the real daily burn (TDEE) to Food goals.
  - Body: one merged weight series plus the smart-scale composition.
  - Mobility: walking speed (≥1.0 m/s, Studenski 2011 JAMA), asymmetry, double support, 6-minute walk.
  - Workouts: Apple workouts with heart-rate curves, matched to Hevy sessions by time overlap so strength sessions finally get heart-rate data.
- **Data prerequisite:** age (birth year), sex and height are not stored anywhere. Add them to the singleton athlete_profile or a new health_profile, or percentiles and BMI context can't be computed.

WHAT'S CURRENTLY UGLY, CRAMPED OR CONFUSING:
- Health sits as the 3rd of 4 tabs under a "Training" page title, with the irrelevant NextSessionBanner below it.
- Overview is just the rings plus a collapsed list of the last 20 workouts, and the list ignores the date control.
- The right rail repeats the section's numbers with different rules, and on phones it drops below the content.
- Charts are 112–160 px tall with 9 px axis ticks, and there are no goal or reference lines anywhere.
- About 18 mini-cards under Steps, each with a permanent description paragraph. The Running cards are all dashes on non-run days.
- Body has two date controls (the page's Day/Week/Month plus the smart scale's 30D/90D/1Y/All) and 3 Apple charts plus 14 smart-scale stat cards.
- Drill-down behaves differently per chart: tooltip link vs pinned popover vs a pointer cursor that does nothing.
- Nothing explains whether a value is good or bad.

ARCHITECTURE FIX FOR THE CONSISTENCY BUGS:
- One `useHealthDaily(metric, from, to)` hook with the aggregation in the query's `select`, so it's memoised.
- Ideally backed by a SQL RPC that does the hour collapse server-side and returns daily/hourly rows.
- One pure `healthWindowStats.ts` holding the window average, the per-metric rule for the in-progress day, the completeness floor and the trend vs the previous window. The section headline, the side panel, the hero and Daily's HealthCard all use it.
- `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` so stepping the date doesn't blank every chart.

findings.title: HealthStatsPanel drops 'today' everywhere: Day mode on today is all dashes, and last night is never counted in sleep stats
findings.evidence: `function completed(series){ const t = todayStr(); return series.filter(d => d.date !== t) }` (HealthStatsPanel.tsx:65-68) is applied by `split()` (:76-82) to every panel. In Day mode buildWindow gives from=to=anchor, so with anchor=today (the default after picking Day) `current` is [] and StepsStats/EnergyStats/HeartStats render 'Steps that day: —', 'Days with data: 0' while the section beside them shows today's real steps. SleepStats (:217) runs the same split over computeSleepSummary, but nights are keyed by the WAKE day (healthAggregate sleepNightKey), so today's key IS last night, a finished night. It is removed from 'Slept that night', every week/month 'Average per night', and from best/shortest night. OverviewStats (:276) also excludes today for steps/energy but not for sleep/HR, so the same panel mixes two rules.
findings.fix: Replace the blanket `completed()` with a per-metric rule. For cumulative activity metrics (sum type), exclude today only from MULTI-day averages and trend comparisons. In Day mode show today's value labelled 'so far'. Never exclude for sleep (the wake-day night is complete) or for 'latest'/'minmaxavg' metrics. Put the rule in one pure helper (e.g. healthWindowStats.ts: `inProgressPolicy(metric)`) and add a sucrase verify script covering Day+today, Week incl. last night, and the Overview mix.

findings.title: Same labelled figure computed by different rules in the section headline, the right panel and Daily — numbers disagree side by side
findings.evidence: Steps 'weekly average': StepsSection.tsx:39-41 `const avgSteps = stepDays.length ? totalSteps / stepDays.length : 0` INCLUDES today's partial day; StepsStats excludes it via split(). Energy: EnergySection.tsx:104-109 `chartData.filter(d => d.date !== today && d.active + d.basal > MIN_COMPLETE_DAY_KCAL)` (1550 kcal floor) vs EnergyStats (:160-168), which excludes today but applies no floor. Sleep: SleepSection periodDetail averages all nights incl. last night; SleepStats drops it (H-01). Heart: HeartStats takes lo/hi from `inWindow` (incl. today, :196) but the average from `dayAvgs` via split (:193, excl. today). Each surface calls useHealthMetricSeries + computeX on its own with its own window (panel uses win.fetchFrom = 2x window). This is the 'same concept, different path' problem the owner described.
findings.fix: Create ONE hook `useHealthDaily(metric, from, to)` that returns the aggregated daily series (aggregation in useQuery `select`), plus ONE pure `healthWindowStats(metric, series, window)` returning {avg, total, best, worst, daysWithData, trendVsPrevious, completeness}. It holds the in-progress-day policy (H-01) and a per-metric completeness floor: basal-driven floor for energy, a wear-time/coverage floor for steps. Section headlines, HealthStatsPanel, the new Health hero and Daily HealthCard all render from it, so a labelled number can only be computed once.

findings.title: Heart Day chart drops to 0 bpm for every hour without samples (incl. all future hours today); '0–0 bpm' headline when Min/Max absent
findings.evidence: computeHeartRateHourlySeries: `const range = rangeFromPoints(byHour.get(h) ?? []) ?? { min: 0, max: 0, avg: 0 }` (healthAggregate.ts:227). HeartSection.tsx:48-49 maps it to `avg: Math.round(r.avg)` and feeds BarLineChart, whose default `yDomain=['auto','auto']` then includes 0. At 10:00 hours 11–23 plot 0 bpm, as do charging hours; the line plunges and the real curve flattens. rangeFromPoints also defaults missing fields to 0 (`min: mins.length ? Math.min(...mins) : 0`, :196). Probe with an Avg-only point returned `{min:0,max:0,avg:70}`, so the Day headline prints `${min}–${max}` = '0–0' and spanMin/lo in HeartSection/HeartStats/OverviewStats become 0.
findings.fix: Return null (not 0) for empty hourly buckets and for missing Min/Max. Type HourlyRange fields as number|null. In HeartSection pass null through, set `connectNulls={false}` on the Line and skip the Bar for null. Filter nulls before Math.min/Math.max (`spanMin`, `lo`/`hi`). Fall back to Avg for min/max only when explicitly labelled. Add assertions to a verify script.

findings.title: 'Latest' mini-cards (VO2 max, 6-min walk, Cardio Recovery, Wrist Temp) only look inside the selected window → VO2 max reads '—' most days
findings.evidence: `if (aggType === 'latest') { const last = series[series.length - 1]; return { value: last?.value ?? null, windowLabel: 'Latest', ... } }` (MetricMiniCard.tsx:51-54). The series comes from `useHealthMetricSeries(metric, window.from, window.to)` (:76), and in Day mode from=to=anchor. Apple writes VO2 max only after qualifying outdoor walks/runs (the card's own description says so), so for this strength-focused user the card shows '—' on almost every day and often in Week mode too, even though a reading exists. That blocks the owner's direct question 'my VO2 is low, how bad is it?'.
findings.fix: For aggType 'latest', fetch a lookback independent of the page window (e.g. 365 days ending at the anchor). Show the newest value with 'from <date>' and a sparkline of all readings. On the new Health page, promote VO2 max to a hero tile with a FRIEND-registry age/sex percentile band. That needs birth year and sex, which are not stored yet: add them to athlete_profile or a health_profile singleton.

findings.title: Sleep stage bar divides by total sleep but also draws Awake → shares sum to >100% and the Awake segment is clipped
findings.evidence: `const pct = detail.total > 0 ? (val / detail.total) * 100 : 0` for every entry of STAGES, which includes `awake` (SleepSection.tsx:347-354). `total` is totalSleep (deep+core+rem, excludes awake), so the widths add up to (deep+core+rem+awake)/total. Probe with core 4, rem 1.5, deep 1, awake 0.8 gives 112.3%. The container is `overflow-hidden`, so the Awake segment is cut off and every other segment is drawn too wide.
findings.fix: Use `const denom = detail.deep + detail.core + detail.rem + detail.awake` as the bar denominator (time in the sleep window). Keep the headline as total sleep. Optionally show % labels in the legend.

findings.title: Hour-level collapse keeps ONE row per UTC hour, destroying minute-grain history (pre 'Time Grouping: Hours' rows) — 3000 steps/hour computed as 50
findings.evidence: `function hourKeyOf(p){ return p.recorded_at.slice(0, 13) }` and collapseIntraStreamMinuteDuplicates keeps a single point per hour for every sum metric. The file's own comment (:13-16) documents that 2026-07-20 data arrived as per-minute samples ('88 of 94 minutes had TWO points'), i.e. before HAE's Hours grouping. The HAE configs in docs/health-auto-export all use exportAggregation=Hours with 'Previous 7 Days' reconciliation, so older minute-grain days were never re-exported. Probe: 60 minute rows of 50 steps in one hour → computeDailySeries returns 50 (real 3000). Any Month/90-day view reaching July 2026, and ai-proxy's collapseDuplicateSumPoints copy, under-reports steps, energy and exercise minutes by ~95%. PLAUSIBLE: not verified against live rows.
findings.fix: Make the collapse grain-aware per hour. If the hour contains a boundary (':00:00') row, or has ≤3 rows with near-identical values (the re-delivery pattern), keep one as today. If it has many distinct minutes and no boundary row (minute grain), dedupe per minute (largest per minute) and SUM. Add this case to scripts/verify-health-source-dedup.cjs and mirror it in ai-proxy. Better: run a one-off count query (with the owner's opt-in) to see which dates are minute-grain.

findings.title: Workouts list downloads 20 full health_workouts rows incl. raw HR curves + GPS routes on every Overview visit, even while collapsed
findings.evidence: `const { data: workouts = [], isLoading } = useHealthWorkouts({ limit: 20 })` is called at the top of WorkoutsList (HealthTab.tsx:75), outside the `expanded` condition. fetchHealthWorkouts does `.select('*')` (healthApi.ts:46), which includes `raw` jsonb holding per-interval `heartRateData`, per-second `route[]` GPS arrays and stepCount arrays. The row only needs name/start/duration/avg HR/active energy; `raw` is only read by HealthWorkoutDetail. The list also ignores the page's date selector and shows no year.
findings.fix: Split into `fetchHealthWorkoutSummaries({from,to})`, selecting id,name,start_time,end_time,duration_seconds,active_energy_kj,avg/max_heart_rate and scoped to the selected window, plus `fetchHealthWorkout(id)`, selecting raw only when the detail opens. Gate the list query with `enabled: expanded` (or show the list un-collapsed on the new page).

findings.title: Query fan-out and duplicated downloads: ~21 paginated select('*') queries for the Steps view, overlapping windows under different keys, aggregation recomputed every render
findings.evidence: Every MetricMiniCard runs its own `useHealthMetricSeries(metric, window.from, window.to)` (MetricMiniCard.tsx:76). Steps renders 13 STEPS_EXTRA + 5 RUNNING cards + 2 section queries + StepsStats' `useHealthMetricSeries('step_count', win.fetchFrom, win.to)` (a 14-day key for a 7-day view, HealthStatsPanel.tsx:140), so step_count is downloaded twice under different keys. SleepSection adds a third sleep key (`daysAgoStr(29), today`, :219). fetchHealthMetricSeries pages sequentially with `select('*')` (id,user_id,synced_at,source_family included, healthApi.ts:100). Components call computeDailySeries/computeSleepSummary inline on every render with no memo; SleepSection calls computeSleepSummary 3× per render. There is no keepPreviousData, so each date step blanks all of it.
findings.fix: (1) Add a SQL RPC `health_series(p_metrics text[], p_from, p_to, p_grain 'hour'|'day')` implementing the hour collapse with DISTINCT ON (metric, date_trunc('hour', recorded_at)), boundary-row first, qty desc. It returns ≤24×days rows, or daily rows, for many metrics in one call. (2) Until then, batch each mini grid into one `.in('metric_name', metrics)` query and narrow the select to metric_name,date,recorded_at,unit,source,value. (3) Move aggregation into useQuery `select` so it's memoised per data reference. (4) Have the side panel and section share one fetch window. (5) Add `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`.

findings.title: Offset pagination ordered only by non-unique recorded_at — rows can be skipped or duplicated at the 1000-row boundary
findings.evidence: `.order('recorded_at', { ascending: true }).range(offset, offset + MAX_ROWS_PER_PAGE - 1)` (healthApi.ts:104-105). The unique key is (user_id, metric_name, recorded_at, source), so ties on recorded_at are routine: the documented duplicate pattern is the same hour under two source strings ('Watch' vs 'Watch|Watch'). Postgres gives no stable order within ties across separate LIMIT/OFFSET requests, so a tie group straddling a page boundary can return one row twice and another never. Duplicates are harmless after the collapse; a skipped hour or HR window is not.
findings.fix: Add a deterministic tiebreaker: `.order('recorded_at').order('id')`. Or better, keyset pagination (`.gt('recorded_at', lastTs)` with an id tiebreak). Moot once the RPC in H-08 lands.

findings.title: Days without data silently vanish from Steps/Energy/Heart/mini charts (x-axis compresses), while Sleep left-joins every date
findings.evidence: StepsSection.tsx:50 `stepDays.map(d => ({ label: fmtDay(d.date), ... }))`, HeartSection.tsx:50 `hrDaily.map(...)` and the EnergySection byDate map (:43-59) only contain dates that have rows. SleepSection deliberately does `datesBetweenStr(chartRange.from, chartRange.to).map(...)` with the comment 'so a night with no synced data still shows as a gap on the axis instead of silently disappearing'. A Watch-off week in a Month view renders as a continuous series with irregular labels.
findings.fix: Add a shared `denseDaily(series, from, to)` helper (datesBetweenStr + null fill) and use it in every daily chart. Render null as a gap (Bar skips; Line `connectNulls={false}`) and optionally a faint 'no data' tick.

findings.title: Chart drill-down is inconsistent and partly unreachable (hover-tooltip links vs pinned popover vs pointer cursor with no handler)
findings.evidence: SleepSection's own comment: 'Links inside a hover tooltip were unreachable in practice — the tooltip re-anchors/hides the moment the mouse moves toward it', so Sleep uses a pinned popover. Steps (`<Tooltip ... content={StepsTooltipContent} wrapperStyle={{ pointerEvents: 'auto' }} />`), Energy and BarLineChart (Heart, mini cards) still put 'Go to this day →' inside that hover tooltip. Energy bars set `cursor={period !== 'day' ? 'pointer' : 'default'}` (:161,166) but have no onClick. BarLineChart's `onPointClick` prop never fires on a click; it only feeds the tooltip button. Stale comments still reference `trigger="click"` (BarLineChart.tsx:106-110, EnergySection.tsx:61-65).
findings.fix: Extract Sleep's pinned-popover pattern into a shared `useChartDrilldown()` plus `<ChartPin>`. Every daily bar chart then gets the same interaction: hover or tap shows values; click pins a popover at the bar with 'View this day' and any per-metric actions. Wire Bar.onClick in BarLineChart to it, drop cursor:pointer where there is no handler, and delete the stale comments.

findings.title: Body weight comes from four sources through different readers — two 'Weight' charts sit in the same Body card and the coaches can disagree
findings.evidence: BodySection plots Apple `weight_body_mass`/`body_fat_percentage`/`body_mass_index` (BodySection.tsx:95-113, with a 'Nd old' stale warning). The same card renders BodyCompositionPanel, whose BODY_COMP_FIELDS again include Weight, Body fat and BMI from body_composition_reports. fetchBodyweightHistory (hevyApi.ts:306-327, Progress) unions hevy_body_measurements + Apple but not the smart scale. useNutritionCoach (:90), Daily HealthCard (:50), BodyStats, ptCoachApi and coachContext read Apple only. If the scale doesn't write to Apple Health (BodySection.tsx:42 alludes to a 'MovingLife/weight gap'), the headline weight is stale while a fresh scan sits one card lower, and the nutrition coach can report 'no bodyweight'.
findings.fix: One `fetchBodyweightSeries(from,to)` returning per-day {date, kg, source} with a precedence: smart-scale report > Hevy manual > Apple, matching the existing 'manual outranks device' rule. Expose it through one `useBodyweight` hook used by Body, Progress, NutritionCoach, HealthCard and both coach contexts. The Body section shows ONE weight chart (7-day moving-average trend + dots coloured by source) and ONE body-fat chart. The smart-scale panel keeps only the fields Apple doesn't have.

findings.title: Heart section charts average heart rate (activity-dependent) while resting HR and HRV — the real health/recovery markers — get only a bare number
findings.evidence: `const chartData = isDay ? computeHeartRateHourlySeries(...).map(r => ({ label: r.label, avg: ... })) : hrDaily.map(r => ({ ..., avg: Math.round(r.avg) }))` goes into `<BarLineChart dataKey="avg" tooltipLabel="Avg heart rate" .../>`. Resting HR and HRV appear only as SideStat numbers ('avg resting', 'avg HRV'), with no trend, no personal baseline and no reference. The panel's trend badge marks avg HR 'down = good', which has no clinical basis for all-day average HR.
findings.fix: Make the main Heart chart a weekly/daily resting-HR trend with a personal 60-day baseline band, plus an HRV (SDNN) trend with a 7-day rolling mean vs baseline ±1 SD (Plews 2013 approach). Show the clinical RHR range (60–100) and population context as a note. Keep the day min–max as a secondary Day-mode view, and remove the 'down is good' badge from average HR.

findings.title: Toothbrushing 'N× that day' and time list count raw rows, not the collapsed series — re-delivered duplicates inflate the count
findings.evidence: `const dayPoints = (showTodayCount || showTodayTimes) ? points.filter(p => p.date === window.to) : []` / `const dayCount = showTodayCount ? dayPoints.length : null` (MetricMiniCard.tsx:80-86) uses the raw `points`. The value above it comes from computeDailySeries, which applies the hour collapse. The hourly re-delivery pattern (2–3 rows per hour) therefore prints '4× that day' and repeated times for two brushings.
findings.fix: Export the collapse helper from healthAggregate (e.g. `collapsedPoints(metric, points)`) and derive dayCount/dayTimes from it. Dedupe times with a Set.

findings.title: Wrist Temp card claims a 'deviation' but shows the latest absolute HealthKit temperature
findings.evidence: `{ metric: 'apple_sleeping_wrist_temperature', title: 'Wrist Temp', unit: '°C', ... description: 'Overnight skin temperature deviation — can flag illness or cycle changes.' }` with aggregation `apple_sleeping_wrist_temperature: 'latest'`. HealthKit's appleSleepingWristTemperature samples are absolute °C. The deviation shown in Apple Health is computed against the user's baseline, so the card prints ~35 °C under a 'deviation' label. PLAUSIBLE: not checked against a live row.
findings.fix: Compute the deviation client-side as the night value minus the median of the previous 30–60 nights (what Apple displays), show it as ±0.x °C with the absolute value in the tooltip, and fix the copy.

findings.title: Loading is indistinguishable from 'no data', and every date step blanks all charts (no keepPreviousData)
findings.evidence: MetricMiniCard ignores isLoading: `{value != null ? value.toFixed(decimals) : '—'}` (:117) shows '—' while fetching, the same as a metric with no rows. useHealthMetricSeries sets no placeholderData, so ‹ › or a period switch empties every chart before the new pages arrive. EnergySection's `isLoading` comes from the anchor-only query (:28), while the chart reads a different range query that can still be loading, so the chart renders empty with no skeleton. That anchor query also runs in Week/Month mode, where it isn't used.
findings.fix: Add `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` to the series hook. Render a Skeleton in cards/charts while `isLoading && !data`. In EnergySection derive the Day figures from the range query (from===to in Day mode) and drop the extra anchor queries.

findings.title: Misleading labels: rolling windows called '(this week)/(this month)', last night called 'Sleep today', Daily says 'steps today' for any date and links to /training
findings.evidence: dateNav.ts:36 `const suffix = isToday ? (period === 'week' ? ' (this week)' : ' (this month)') : ''` labels a rolling last-7/last-30-day window, which often spans two months. SleepSection.tsx:193 `anchor === today ? 'Sleep today' : ...` for the night that ended this morning. HealthCard.tsx:64 `<Sub>steps today</Sub>` is shown for whatever `date` Daily is viewing, and :56 `<CellLink to="/training">`. HealthTab.tsx:170 `onChange={p => { setPeriod(p); setAnchor(today) }}` throws away the browsed date whenever the period changes.
findings.fix: Use 'Last 7 days' / 'Last 30 days' (or real calendar week/month options), 'Last night' / 'Night of <date>', and 'steps' or 'steps on <date>'. Point Daily's link to the new /health route (deep-link to the matching section). Keep the anchor when the period changes, clamped to today.

findings.title: Workout route map is stretched: lat and lon are scaled independently; the cos(lat) correction in the comment is not applied
findings.evidence: Comment: '// Keep aspect roughly correct: lon degrees shrink by cos(lat).' The code does `const sx = (lon) => PAD + ((lon - minLon) / lonRange) * (W - 2 * PAD)` and `const sy = (lat) => PAD + (1 - (lat - minLat) / latRange) * (H - 2 * PAD)` (:62-65), so each axis is stretched to fill 320×200 independently. At Oslo's ~60°N every route is distorted, and a near-straight N–S walk with a few metres of GPS jitter becomes a full-width zigzag.
findings.fix: Project to local metres (x = lon·cos(meanLat), y = lat), take one scale = min((W-2P)/xRange, (H-2P)/yRange) and centre the path.

findings.title: Manual sleep rows are stamped source_family='apple' by the column default
findings.evidence: upsertManualSleepEntry builds rows with `source: 'manual'` and `value.source: 'manual'` (healthApi.ts:149-163) but no `source_family`. Migration 062 declares `source_family text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'apple'`, so every manual correction is labelled Apple, contradicting the HealthMetric type comment 'every row is apple except a manual correction' and CLAUDE.md.
findings.fix: Add `source_family: 'manual'` to each row. Optionally backfill: `UPDATE health_metrics SET source_family='manual' WHERE source='manual'`.

findings.title: Sleep Day view mixes a manual override with Watch sessions; source tooltip keys on a different date than the bars
findings.evidence: computeSleepSummary lets a manual entry win for a night, but `const daySessions = dayDetail ? extractSleepSessions(points, anchor) : []` (:171) still draws the Watch session timeline, so the headline (manual total) and the 'When you slept' band (Watch) describe different data. `sourcesByDate` is keyed by `p.date` (:209-214) while the bars and summary are keyed by sleepNightKey (the sleepEnd date), so the 'Manual' pill and tooltip sources can attach to the wrong night whenever the two differ.
findings.fix: When the night has manual rows, hide the timeline or caption it 'Watch data, replaced by your manual entry'. Export sleepNightKey from healthAggregate and key sourcesByDate by it.

findings.title: Dead code, duplicated helpers and stale comments in the Health module
findings.evidence: `useHealthMetrics` / `fetchHealthMetrics` (a 5000-row select('*')) and `qk.health.metrics` have zero call sites. `dateNav.shiftStr` duplicates `shiftDateStr` in shared/utils/dateUtils. `daysBetween` is defined in both BodySection and HealthStatsPanel. `fmtDay` exists in 6 files with 3 different formats. `fmtDuration` is in HealthTab and HealthWorkoutDetail. `mean`/`avg` are defined in 3 places. HealthTab keeps an uncontrolled fallback (`localSection`, `useAnchorDate()`, `localPeriod`) that TrainingPage always overrides, so the tab runs two anchor timers. Stale comments: HealthTab.tsx:158-160 ('SourceToggle deliberately stays per-section' — deleted), BarLineChart/EnergySection 'trigger="click"', BodySection.tsx:42 refers to a 'header comment on the MovingLife/weight gap' that doesn't exist.
findings.fix: Delete the dead hook, API function and key. Move date/format/mean helpers into one `health/format.ts` (reuse shiftDateStr). When Health becomes its own page, keep ONE owner of section/range state (the page) and drop the controlled/uncontrolled dual path. Remove or rewrite the stale comments.

findings.title: Mini-card grids are walls: ~18 cards under Steps with permanent descriptions; Running cards are em dashes on non-run days
findings.evidence:
STEPS_EXTRA_METRICS has 13 entries and RUNNING_EXTRA_METRICS 5 (miniMetrics.ts notes they have 'currently two rows each'). Every card permanently prints `

{description}

` (MetricMiniCard.tsx:130). In the phone's 2-column grid that is ~9 rows of tall cards, mostly '—' for running dynamics, stair speeds and pushes. There are no reference ranges, so the descriptions can't say whether a value is good.
findings.fix: Show only cards with data in the window. Fold the rest into a 'Not recorded in this window (N)' disclosure. Move descriptions into an InfoBubble. Give the useful gait metrics a reference note (walking speed ≥1.0 m/s, Studenski 2011; asymmetry/double-support 'lower is steadier') and move them to a 'Mobility' section on the new page.

findings.title: No ErrorBoundary around Health sections or the free-form HAE workout detail
findings.evidence: HealthWorkoutDetail renders free-form jsonb straight into JSX, e.g. `{raw.location && ` · ${raw.location}`}` (:124). CLAUDE.md's ErrorBoundary rule: 'Wrap any surface whose data shape is not contractually guaranteed'. HAE's payload shape is explicitly undocumented and varies by field (numOrQty). An object-valued field would throw during render and blank the whole Training page, since none of the Health sections or the modal is wrapped.
findings.fix: Wrap each Health section and the HealthWorkoutDetail body in the shared ErrorBoundary. Guard free-form fields with `typeof === 'string'` before rendering.
